mathematical_results.statement: Four-term bimodule Koszul formula computes Ext(DB,M). The ordinary iterations are path components of the explicitly presented tensor algebra. Once the first step is pure, later obstructions are ordinary higher Tors of tensor powers. A finite leading-triple count certifies the quadratic PBW branch in all degrees.

Every standard AS object has rho>=4. In rank four every adjacent point correspondence has positive dimension. At rank five a finite correspondence requires the two cubic-minor span dimensions to sum to at most 20, including nonreduced intersections. For rho four the point scheme is a fiber product of kernel and image plane maps. Constant-plane fibers have the listed full-column-rank Kronecker types; a moving plane yields paired lines on the determinant surfaces. Both determinant quartics cannot be smooth.

No standard AS object has rho four. A matched binary central slice has a concise full-rank rectangular pencil at every parameter. Twelve restriction rank checks force point fibers and L3 pencils. A moving ruling sweeps a smooth Segre quadric, and simultaneous kernel and cokernel cubics factor the two coefficient nets through 3-by-3 isomorphisms. The adjacent cut then has rank nine instead of six. At rho five at least two of the four adjacent point correspondences have positive dimension. Four finite correspondences of a finite-Frobenius candidate glue scheme-theoretically into unique point sequences of length-twenty parameter schemes. At any rho the row-plane map of the rank-two evaluation locus has point fibers, by a growth quotient of dimension at least 12^m.

At rho five, a rank-three evaluation has at most one point neighbor on either side and cannot have both. Each coefficient space must contain a hypersurface swept by planes of matrices of rank at most two. Hyperplanes and upper rank three are excluded, and a rank-four determinant quadratic forces the unique five-matrix form with diagonal blocks S and adj(S). Its matching opposite binary evaluation planes force exponential growth. Hence the AS lower bound is six, attained by the polynomial ring.

At rho six all finite edge point schemes have identity four-step shift; three consecutive finite edges already give length-twenty four-periodic sequences. On the finite branch, three ordered four-spaces in the finite Gorenstein coordinate algebra determine indexed isomorphism up to units and algebra isomorphism. Opposite square spaces agree after unit normalization. A reduced symmetric CI has an isolated normalized third-space solution for a fixed first window. An equivalent ratio search lies in P(D/k) of dimension eighteen: a ten-by-ten multiplication matrix has rank six, its kernel recovers the next coordinate space up to a unique unit scaling class. A second control uses a nonreduced length-twenty ring. On the reduced example the multiplication rank locus has distinct five-dimensional components from the two coordinate flags and a six-coordinate support, with tangent rank 13 at their test points. The transporter rejects the opposite-flag component generically; the support component has no genuine ratios.

The complete projective square-root fiber at the symmetric twenty points consists of 2^19 reduced sign translates, including all possible degenerate candidates. The property persists on an open neighborhood. A general first relation space has no all-four-finite AS extension. With both projections rigid, any such AS extension has period dividing two, cubic wedge rank 20 and a unique invertible generator of the double alternation kernel.
